t: Liu Yu, a general of the Jin who had retaken Chang'an and Luoyang, received the abdication of Sima Dewen in 420 and founded the Song dynasty.
The Reign of Yuanjia (425–453) under Emperor Wen is remembered as one of the relative golden ages of the Southern Dynasties.
Failed wars against Northern Wei and murderous succession struggles weakened the dynasty until Xiao Daocheng took the throne as Emperor of Qi in 479.
dyk: The astronomer Zu Chongzhi, who lived in the Liu Song period, is noted for calculating pi to seven decimal places.
ev: Liu Yu captures the Southern Yan capital at Guanggu, ending Southern Yan
Sima Dewen abdicates in favour of Liu Yu, who founds the Song dynasty
The Reign of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen brings prosperity and stable administration
Emperor Wen's great invasion of Northern Wei ends in disaster, and the provinces south of the Yellow River are laid waste
The heir apparent Liu Shao assassinates Emperor Wen and is overthrown by his brother Liu Jun, Emperor Xiaowu
Liu Ziye succeeds his father and rules as a tyrant until his uncle assassinates him
Xiao Daocheng takes the throne as Emperor of Qi, ending the Liu Song
